 The Honourable Smt. Justice M.G.Priyadarsini
 M.A.C.M.A.No.3129 Of 2016
Judgment:

1. Dissatisfied with the compensation awarded by the learned Motor Vehicle Accidents Claims Tribunal-cum-X Additional Chief Judge, City Civil Court, Hyderabad (for short, "the Tribunal") in M.V.O.P.No.1736 of 2013, dated 18.04.2016, the claimant /injured preferred the present Appeal seeking enhancement of compensation amount.

entities.text: Motor Vehicle Accidents Claims Tribunal-cum-X Additional Chief Judge, City Civil Court, Hyderabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. For the sake of convenience, the parties herein are referred as they were arrayed before the Tribunal.

3. The brief facts of the case are that initially, the petitioner/injured filed a petition under Section 166 of M.V.Act, 1988 and Rule 455 of A.P.M.V.Rules, 1989 r/w. Section 140(c) of M.V.Act, seeking compensation of Rs.6,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by her in a motor vehicle accident that occurred on 11.03.2013.

It is stated by the petitioner that on 11.03.2013, at about 1.00 p.m., when the petitioner/injured was travelling in Auto Trolley bearing No.AP-23Y-3930 along with Tomato load and when the said Auto reached at Gandimaisamma X Roads, the driver of one Auto Trolley bearing No.AP-28-TV-0616 drove the said vehicle in a rash and negligent manner at high speed and dashed the Auto Trolley in which the petitioner/injured was travelling.

As a result, MGP,J the petitioner sustained Head injury, blunt injury to chest and pelvis, fracture ribs 3, 4 and 5 (right)
fracture of scapula (right), fracture of Rami (right), which are grievous in nature and other multiple injuries all over the body and incurred an amount of Rs.2,50,000/- towards medical expenses.

4. Based on a complaint, Police of Dundigal Police Station registered a case in Crime No.186 of 2013 under Sections 304-A and 337 of IPC against the driver of crime Auto.
5.
It is stated by the petitioner/injured that she was 50 years old at the time of accident and used to earn Rs.9,000/- per month as a Vegetable Vendor.

Due to the injuries sustained by her in the alleged accident, she was unable to do her vegetable selling business as it requires constant mobility,
lifting and other manual laborious work.
As such, she was put to severe hardship and monitory loss.

Hence, filed claim petition seeking compensation of Rs.6,00,000 against the respondent Nos.1 & 2,
who are the owner and insurer of crime Auto Trolley.
6. Respondent No.1, owner of the crime Auto Trolley Bearing No.AP-28-TV-0616, remained ex-parte.

7. Respondent No.2/Insurance Company filed its counter denying the averments made in the claim petition including, MGP,J involvement of the vehicle, occurrence of accident, age, earnings of the petitioner, injuries sustained to her and treatment undergone by the injured.

It also contended that L Laxmi, Medak Dist vs M Durga Goud Allipuram, Sangareddy And ... on 10 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/128563142/
1 the driver of the Auto Trolley in which petitioner had travelled do not possess valid license to drive the said vehicle.

sentences.text: As such, the Insurance Company is not liable to pay any compensation.

8. Based on the pleadings made by both the parties, the learned Tribunal had framed the following issues:-
(i) Whether the petitioner sustained injuries in the accident on 11.03.2013 due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of crime Auto bearing No.AP-28TV-0616?
(ii) Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation and if so, to what quantum and to whom such quantum is recoverable?

(iii) To what relief?
9.

Before the Tribunal, the petitioner/injured, in order to substantiate her claim, got examined herself as PW1 and also got examined PW2-Doctor and got marked Exs.A1 to A6 along with Exs.X1 to X3 on her behalf.
On behalf of Respondent No.2/Insurance Company, no witness was examined, however, Ex.B1-Copy of Insurance Policy was marked with consent.

10. After considering the oral and documentary evidence available on record, the learned Tribunal had partly allowed the claim petition of the petitioner/injured by awarding compensation MGP,J of Rs.1,61,000/- along with interest @ 7.5% per annum from the date of petition till the date of realization payable by both the Respondent Nos.1 & 2 jointly and severally.
Having not satisfied with the compensation awarded, the petitioner/injured preferred the present Appeal seeking enhancement of the same.

11. Heard arguments of Sri T.Viswarupa Chary, learned counsel for the appellant/injured and Sri Kondadi Ajay Kumar, learned Standing Counsel for Respondent No.2/Insurance Company.
Perused the record.

12. The contentions of the learned Counsel for appellant/injured are that the learned Tribunal erred in assessing the disability sustained to her @ 20% as against the Disability Certificate issued under Ex.X1.
He also contended that the learned Tribunal ought to have considered the loss of earning capacity of the petitioner @ 100% as she is incapable of doing her work as a vegetable vendor.

It is further contended that the learned Tribunal ought to have considered the earnings of a vegetable vendor @ Rs.6,000/- per month by following the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Syed Sadiq v. United India Insurance Co.Ltd. (2014) 2 SCC 735 and further contended that the learned Tribunal ought to have considered the age of the petitioner/injured as 55 instead of 50 and ought to have awarded future prospects to the income of the MGP,J deceased and therefore prayed to allow the Appeal by enhancing the compensation amount.

On the other hand, learned counsel for respondent No.2/Insurance Company contended that the learned Tribunal, after considering all the aspects, had awarded adequate compensation and interference of this Court is not necessary.

14. Now the point that emerges for determination is ,
(i).
Whether the order passed by the learned Tribunal requires interference of this Court?
(ii) Whether the petitioner/injured is entitled for enhancement of compensation?
POINT:-

15. A perusal of the record shows that the petitioner/injured examined herself as PW1 and reiterated the contents of the claim petition and deposed about the manner of accident and injuries sustained to her.
To prove the injuries sustained by her, she got examined PW2-Orthopaedic Surgeon.

PW2 in his evidence deposed that the petitioner/injured approached their Hospital with the following injures:- (1) Fracture 3rd, 4th and 5th ribs right; (2) Fracture of Scapula and (3) Fracture of Pelvis.

After making thorough examination of Medical record of the petitioner, he issued Ex.X1-Disability Certificate as per Mc bride scale assessing the disability of the petitioner @ 30% which is partial and permanent MGP,J in nature.
He further stated that the petitioner incurred permanent functional disability and cannot undertake agricultural operations on account of the injuries sustained by her.
During his cross-examination, he admitted that he had not treated the patient, but he only assessed the disability sustained to her as per Mc.bride scale.
16. Apart from oral evidence, the petitioner/injured also adduced documentary evidence under Exs.A1 to A6.

Ex.A1- FIR shows that Police of Dundigal Police Station, Cyberabad District,
registered a case in Crime No.186 of 2013 under Sections 304-A and 337 IPC, conducted investigation and filed charge sheet under Ex.A2 against the driver of crime Auto Trolley bearing No.AP-28-TV-0616.

entities.text: Police of Dundigal Police Station, Cyberabad District
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
Ex.A3 is the Medico Legal Record issued by MNR Medical College Hospital,
Sangareddy, which discloses that the petitioner sustained (1) Injury to forehead, (2) Injury to right cheek, (3) Pain on right shoulder and right hip (4) Fractures of 3rd, 4th, 5th ribs, (5) Fracture of superior inferior public rami and (6) fracture of right scapula, suprapubic rami and the said injuries are grievous in nature.

Ex.A4 is the Discharge Summary issued by RR Hospitals wherein the petitioner/injured was diagnosed for RTA-Head injury, blunt injury chest and pelvis and fracture of ribs 3, 4, 5, fracture of scapula and fracture of pelvis inferior rami.
Ex.A5 is the MRI MGP,J Lambar Spine and Ex.A6 are the X-ray reports.
Ex . X1
is the Handicapped Certificate issued by Consultant Orthopedic Surgeon assessing the disability sustained by the petitioner as "30%"
. Ex .
X2 is the X-ray film and Ex.X3 is the Medical prescription 17.

Therefore, from the above oral evidence of PWs1 & 2 coupled with the documentary evidence under Exs.A1 to A6 and Exs.X1 to X3, it can be safely concluded that the petitioner sustained grievous fracture injuries in an accident that occurred on 11.03.2013 due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of crime Auto Trolley bearing No.AP-28TV-0616 which finding of the Tribunal attained finality and requires no interference by this Court.

sentences.text:
The first and foremost contention of the learned counsel for the appellant/injured as stated in the grounds of Appeal is that though the petitioner/injured sustained disability @ 30% as per Ex.X1-Disability Certificate, but the learned Tribunal assessed the said disability @ 20% as against the Disability Certificate issued under Ex.X1.
19.

In this regard, it is pertinent to refer to the evidence of PW2, an Orthopedic Surgeon who deposed that the petitioner sustained 1) Fracture of 3rd, 4th and 5th right ribs; (2) Fracture of Scapula and (3) Fracture of Pelvis and assessed her disability @ 30% and issued MGP,J Ex.X1-Disabiltiy Certificate.
He also stated that the petitioner incurred permanent functional disability and cannot undertake agricultural operations on account of the injuries sustained by her.

20. Therefore, considering the evidence of PW2, Ex.X1-Disability Certificate, fracture injuries sustained by the petitioner which are termed as grievous in nature and also the nature of work being performed by her as a Vegetable Vendor which involves lifting and constant mobility of goods from one place to another, this Court is inclined to interfere with the finding of the learned Tribunal and hereby consider the disability sustained by the petitioner @ 30% as per Ex.X1-Disability Certificate.

21. It is further contended by the learned counsel for the appellant/injured that the learned Tribunal ought to have considered the earnings of a vegetable vendor @ Rs.6,000/- per month by following the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Syed Sadiq v. United India Insurance Co.Ltd. (2014) 2 SCC 735.
22.

entities.text: Syed Sadiq v. United India Insurance Co.Ltd. (2014) 2 SCC 735
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In this regard, it is pertinent to state that though the petitioner/injured contended that she is a vegetable vendor, she did not produce any license showing that she was doing such business.

Hence,
this Court, taking into consideration the cost of living as on the date of accident, is inclined to fix the monthly MGP,J income of the deceased @ Rs.4,500/- per month by interfering with the finding of the learned Tribunal.

23. It is also contended by the learned counsel for the appellant/injured that the Tribunal ought to have considered the age of the injured as 50 years and ought to have applied multiplier 13 and calculated the compensation.
24.
A perusal of the documents filed under Exs.A3 to A5 viz., Medico Legal Record, Discharge Summary and MRI Lambar Spine discloses the age of the injured as 55 years.
Hence, the learned Tribunal took the age of the injured as 55 years and calculated compensation which this Court finds the same to be justified and needs no interference of the same.
Hence, the contention of the appellant/injured is unsustainable in this regard.

25. As far as the contention regarding awarding of future prospects is concerned, it is pertinent to state that though PW2 stated that the petitioner incurred permanent functional disability and cannot undertake agricultural operations on account of the injuries sustained by her, there is no whisper with regard to reduction of any income of PW1 on account of these injuries.

Even PW2 L Laxmi, Medak Dist vs M Durga Goud Allipuram, Sangareddy And ... on 10 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/128563142/
4 deposed that patient (injured) incurred permanent functional disability for her agricultural profession.

entities.text: L Laxmi, Medak Dist vs M Durga Goud Allipuram, Sangareddy
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: But, as per the version of MGP,J petitioner/injured, she is the vegetable vendor.
Moreover, her functional disability is only to the extent of agricultural profession.
It is not the case of petitioner that she cannot attend any work and it implies that she can do any other works.

Though PW1/injured deposed that she is unable to do her work on account of her disability, the injuries sustained by her are not permanent in nature and there is every possibility of recovering from those injuries.
It is settled law
that future prospects can be claimed in accident cases involving serious injuries resulting in permanent disablement.
Thus, the petitioner is not entitled for any future prospects.

26. In view of the above discussion, this Court is inclined to modify the impugned judgment and calculate the compensation as indicated below:-
Loss of income on account of disability = income of the injured x 12 x percentage of disability x relevant multiplier = 4,500 x 12 x 30%x11 = Rs.1,78,200/-
27.

It is also pertinent to mention that the learned Tribunal had awarded an amount of Rs.10,000/-
towards transport charges, an amount of Rs.12,000/- for loss of income during the period of MGP,J treatment and an amount of Rs.60,000/- towards pain and suffering which this Court finds the same to be reasonable and is not inclined to interfere with the same.
Hence, the appellant/injured is entitled for compensation as detailed under.
Name of the Head Awarded by Awarded by S.No. Tribunal this Court 1.

Monthly income Rs.3000/- Rs.4,500/-
 Percentage of 20% 30%
2. disability  Multiplier adopted 11 - 3.
 Transport and other Rs.10,000/- -

4. miscellaneous  expenses  Loss of income during Rs.12,000/- -
5. the period of  treatment  Pain and suffering, Rs.60,000/- -
6. loss of amenities and  expectation of life  TOTAL Rs.1,61,000/- Rs.2,60,200/-

5 28.

As far as interest on the compensation amount is concerned, the learned Tribunal awarded interest @ 7.5% per annum from the date of petition till the date of realization which this Court finds reasonable and is not inclined to interfere with the same .

29. As far as liability is concerned, as Ex.B1-Insurance policy was in force as on the date of accident and in the absence of rebuttal evidence on behalf of respondents, this Court is of the considered MGP,J opinion that the Tribunal had rightly fixed the liability upon respondents 1 & 2 in paying the compensation amount.

30. In the result, M.A.C.M.A.No.3129 of 2016 filed by the appellant/injured is partly-allowed by enhancing the compensation amount awarded by the Tribunal from Rs.1,61,000/- to Rs.2,60,200/-
which shall carry interest @ 7.5% per annum from the date of petition till the date of realization payable by both the respondent Nos.1 & 2 jointly and severally within a period of two months from the date of receipt of a copy of this order.
Upon such deposit, the appellant/injured is entitled to withdraw the same without furnishing any security.
There shall be no order as to costs.
31. Miscellaneous applications, if any, pending shall stand closed.
